/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 14 April 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2354 (104)
Baltic Capesize Index: 3671 (234)
Baltic Panamax Index: 1900 (38)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1344 (24)
Baltic Handysize Index: 706 (5)
CAPESIZE
The market gathered further momentum today, with the BCI 182 5TC climbing by $2,125 to settle at $33,295, supported by firm gains across both basins. The Pacific saw C5 advance by $0.690 to $13.080, while C3 surged by $1.40 to $31.855, reflecting stronger sentiment particularly in the Atlantic. In the Pacific, despite a relatively measured start to the week, sentiment has clearly firmed, underpinned by steady volumes and the presence of three miners active on C5. Early offers around $13.00 saw initial fixtures concluded at $12.80 from a miner, but confidence built through the day, with operators ultimately paying up to $13.40 by the close. The Atlantic basin was the main driver of today’s gains, with activity picking up significantly out of South Brazil and West Africa to China. A series of fixtures were reported in the $31.75 to $32.00 range across various laycans, with offers on the follows for early May arrivals said to be at $32.00.
PANAMAX
Today we have seen more of an active day across both basins. In the Atlantic, although the tonnage list, especially off the Continent, is still apparent the offers are holding with some suggesting that owners are taking a pause and waiting for the bids to come up closer their levels. The P1A reflected this by increasing $304 to $13,459. Minerals supply is playing a significant role within the Atlantic and for fronthaul the same can be echoed along with grains. In Asia, Australian round voyages and Indonesian supply have pushed the market with some market participants suggesting the tonnage count in April is starting to diminish with a relatively healthy supply of cargo. This increase in appetite for open tonnage has been reflected on the period market with reported activity seen today. The P5TC boosted a further $344 to conclude at $17,101.

Asia
HC Energy (73,594 2006) open in Dongguan 21/23 April was to have fixed, although some suggestions that she may still be on subjects, for a trip via Indonesia to South China at $16,500 but the charterer remained unknown. Similarly, the Sea Glory (92,928 2011) open Tianjin 14 April was said to have fixed a North China to Indonesia and the BBG Hong Kong (81,996 2022) open Cailan 13 April fixed an Australian stem to India both with further details lacking.
SUPRAMAX
Another day of upward momentum. The Atlantic overall was positive, there was talk that ultras were seeing in the mid $20,000s from the US Gulf for fronthaul business but no actual fixtures came to light. Also, gains were seen from the South Atlantic as demand remained also for the larger Panamax sector from the area. The Continent-Mediterranean remained rather lacklustre, and brokers said that little fresh enquiry was being seen. From Asia, following on from yesterday fresh activity emerged helping rates to improve. The Astrid Schulte (61,255 2014) open Zhuhai 21/22 April was heard fixed at $25,000 for a trip to Bangladesh but no more details emerged. The Young Harmony (63,567 2014) open Chittagong 22 April was heard fixed via Indonesia trip India at $20,000 again no more details came to light. The Ultra Courage (63,633 2019) Cai Mep 18/20 April fixed trip a via Indonesia redelivery Bangladesh at $25,000. The QC Isabella (63,425 2024) open Chittagong was also heard to have been placed on subjects via Indonesia redelivery Continent with a split rate of $14,250 intention steels but further details remained under wraps. The Ocean Outstanding (63,562 2018) open Quanzhou 13/15 April also fixed a backhaul redelivery West Africa at $16,500. Period activity surfaced, the BBG Baise (61,180 2021) open Luoyuan 13 April was heard to have been placed on subjects for 3/5 months at $19,000 by Daifu. Also, the Ever Success (58,086 2011) open Hong Kong 12 April was on subjects for 5/6 months trading at $17,500. The 11TC average finished the day up $307 at $16,988.

HANDYSIZE
Following on from the previous day, the market experienced another subdued session with limited activity reported. The BHSI rose by 5 points to 706, while the 7TC average increased by $82 to $12,708. In the Continent and Mediterranean, conditions remained flat with little visible activity. The US Gulf appeared relatively balanced, showing minimal fluctuation. In the South Atlantic, rates continued to firm despite a lack of reported fixtures and limited fresh information. Similarly, in Asia, the market remained supported, with sources noting tight prompt tonnage and a steady flow of cargoes. The New Optima (39,042 2019) open Nansha was heard fixed for a trip to Japan with wood pellets at $15,000 by Swire. Additionally, a 30,000 vessel was reported fixed for a trip from Vung Tau via Weda to Ningde at around $5,000 by Lynux, though further details were not disclosed.

Market Fundamentals
CMRG-BHP Deal Reported

China's state iron ore buyer CMRG has reportedly lifted a six-month procurement ban on BHP's key Pilbara grades following high-level talks between BHP's outgoing CEO Mike Henry, incoming CEO Brandon Craig and China Baowu's chairman in Shanghai, newswires report. CMRG, established in 2022 to centralise iron ore buying and extract better terms from miners, had progressively tightened curbs since September 2025. The resolution likely involves pricing concessions, with rivals Rio Tinto and Fortescue already trialling alternative indexes. The ban had contributed to spot market tightness despite record portside stockpiles, keeping seaborne iron ore above the $100/t psychological floor. BHP shares rallied 3.8% on the news while Singapore Exchange benchmark May iron ore was trading at $103.5/t, down 1.2% on the day.

Chinese Dry Bulk Trade

Chinese iron ore imports rose 10.8 Mt from the same period last year to 104.7 Mt in March, bringing first quarter imports 29.4 Mt higher than last year at 314.8 Mt, preliminary customs data show.

Coal imports edged 0.3 Mt higher year-on-year to 39.1 Mt, with 1q26 imports up 1.5 Mt on the year at 116.3 Mt.

First quarter steel imports eased 0.2 Mt on the year to 1.3 Mt while exports fell 2.7 Mt to 24.7 Mt.

Meanwhile, soybean imports lifted 0.5 Mt on the year to 4.0 Mt in March, although posted an equivalent decline to 16.6 Mt in the first three months of the year.

Trading Commentary
Cape
The cape curve pushed up today on the back of higher physical fixtures particularly on c3 and in the Atlantic. Apr traded from a low of 29000 up to a high of 30000 settling around 29800, May moved up from 32250 to 33750. Jun also improved from 32500 to 33600, with Q2 trading 31000 to 32200. Further out, Q3 went from 30400 to 31000, while Q4 moved up from 30350 to 30900. On the back end, Cal 27 traded between 25750 and 25900, with Cal 28 printing twice around 23300. Overall, it was a strong day for capes, with improvements seen right across the curve.

PMX
PMX papers saw an active session today, with prices pushing higher across the curve. Apr traded from a low of 17450 in the morning being paid up to 17650, while May improved from 19400 to 19675. Jun also pushed higher from 19650 to 19900, with Q2 trading 18750 to 19100, Q3 went from 18600 to 18900, while Q4 moved up from 17100 to 17300. On the back end, Cal 27 traded between 14825 and 14900, with Cal 28 trading around 13900, improving around 50 on the day, and Cal 29 printing once at 13650. Overall, the market saw a firm move higher across the curve, with good participation through the session.

SMX + HANDY
The SMX market was well supported as the curve stepped up amid robust buying interest over the day. Apr traded 15450 – 15600, May 17100 – 17400, Jun 16950 – 17350 and the Q2 16550 – 16750. Q3 changed hands between 16500 – 16700, Q4 15400 and Q1 at 12000. Cal27 oscillated between 13075 – 13150 while Cal28 traded 12200. The Handy market followed suit, trading higher with the May trading 15400, Jun at 15250 and Cal27 at 12400.

Carbon
Carbon markets rallied 3% today, reflecting broader markets expectations of imminent peace in the Middle East. This sentiment also contributed to a steep decline in regional energy prices, with prompt month TTF gas decreasing 14%. During the assessment window, the benchmark Dec26 contract was trading at �74.86/eua, up �2.24.

Typically, carbon allowances are positively correlated with European energy prices and broadly reflect demand-side growth. However, currently, this correlation has reversed due to concerns that higher energy prices resulting from energy shortages will curtail industrial and electricity output, thereby lowering demand for carbon allowances.

Market Fundamentals
CMRG-BHP Deal Reported
China's state iron ore buyer CMRG has reportedly lifted a six-
month procurement ban on BHP's key Pilbara grades
following high-level talks between BHP's outgoing CEO Mike
Henry, incoming CEO Brandon Craig and China Baowu's
chairman in Shanghai, newswires report. CMRG, established
in 2022 to centralise iron ore buying and extract better terms
from miners, had progressively tightened curbs since
September 2025. The resolution likely involves pricing
concessions, with rivals Rio Tinto and Fortescue already
trialling alternative indexes. The ban had contributed to spot
market tightness despite record portside stockpiles, keeping
seaborne iron ore above the $100/t psychological ﬂoor. BHP
shares rallied 3.8% on the news while Singapore Exchange
benchmark May iron ore was trading at $103.5/t, down 1.2%
on the day.
Chinese Dry Bulk Trade
Chinese iron ore imports rose 10.8 Mt from the same period
last year to 104.7 Mt in March, bringing ﬁrst quarter imports
29.4 Mt higher than last year at 314.8 Mt, preliminary
customs data show.
Coal imports edged 0.3 Mt higher year-on-year to 39.1 Mt,
with 1q26 imports up 1.5 Mt on the year at 116.3 Mt.
First quarter steel imports eased 0.2 Mt on the year to 1.3 Mt
while exports fell 2.7 Mt to 24.7 Mt.
Meanwhile, soybean imports lifted 0.5 Mt on the year to 4.0
Mt in March, although posted an equivalent decline to 16.6
Mt in the ﬁrst three months of the year.
Trading Commentary
Cape
The cape curve pushed up today on the back of higher
physical ﬁxtures particularly on c3 and in the Atlantic. Apr
traded from a low of 29000 up to a high of 30000  settling
around 29800, May moved up from 32250 to 33750. Jun also
improved from 32500 to 33600, with Q2 trading 31000 to
32200. Further out, Q3 went from 30400 to 31000, while Q4
moved up from 30350 to 30900. On the back end, Cal 27
traded between 25750 and 25900, with Cal 28 printing twice
around 23300. Overall, it was a strong day for capes, with
improvements seen right across the curve.
PMX
PMX papers saw an active session today, with prices pushing
higher across the curve. Apr traded from a low of 17450 in
the morning being paid up to 17650, while May improved
from 19400 to 19675. Jun also pushed higher from 19650 to
19900, with Q2 trading 18750 to 19100, Q3 went from 18600
to 18900, while Q4 moved up from 17100 to 17300. On the
back end, Cal 27 traded between 14825 and 14900, with Cal
28 trading around 13900, improving around 50 on the day,
and Cal 29 printing once at 13650. Overall, the market saw a
ﬁrm move higher across the curve, with good participation
through the session.
SMX + HANDY

amid robust buying interest over the day. Apr traded 15450 –
15600, May 17100 – 17400, Jun 16950 – 17350 and the Q2
16550 – 16750. Q3 changed hands between 16500 – 16700,
Q4 15400 and Q1 at 12000. Cal27 oscillated between 13075 –

Carbon
Carbon markets rallied 3% today, reﬂecting broader markets
expectations of imminent peace in the Middle East. This
sentiment also contributed to a steep decline in regional
energy prices, with prompt month TTF gas decreasing 14%.
During the assessment window, the benchmark Dec26
contract was trading at €74.86/eua, up €2.24.

European energy prices and broadly reﬂect demand-side
growth. However, currently, this correlation has reversed due
to concerns that higher energy prices resulting from energy
shortages will curtail industrial and electricity output,
thereby lowering demand for carbon allowances.

Capesize Report14th April 2026
PAC: Firming         ATL: Very Busy
Market Comments
After all majors remained unﬁxed yesterday – the basin welcomed three majors
out of West Australia today and one out of TRMT to kick oﬀ activity. Initially,
same levels as yesterday were oﬀered with $13.00’s being seen by the majors –
until ﬁnally ﬁrst to ﬁx was the Dampier major for 28/30 April dates at $12.80.
meanwhile, a major out of Hedland was rumored to have concluded at $13.00
and an operator for 27/29 April was last bidding $12.50 and ﬁxed at an
undisclosed rate. Additionally, the major out of TMRT ﬁxed their stem for 22/24
April at high $8.00’s for a trip to Bohadopi. Positivity from yesterday trickled
into this morning with paper gaining momentum and immense volumes
concluded early doors out of the South. The main focus from the get go was
once again mid-May dates with a trader ﬁxing at $31.75 until these dates were
then ﬁxed again a handful of times by traders at $31.50 with one Greek owners
vessel securing $32.00. Additionally, a Newcastlemax ﬁxed for delivery Mundra
20 April via Brazil for redelivery China at $43,500 - equivalent to around high
$30s on C3 basis. Much like the other basins, the North Atlantic saw activity
pick up. A trip from Nouadhibou to Arzew for 01/10 May ﬁxed at $8.40 which as
a Gibraltar round voyage ran to around mid $32k’s. Into the afternoon, a North
Atlantic vessel took an end-users cargo out of Kamsar at $28 for 03/09 May.
This ran to $69,750 for 55 days and a $1.8mil score excluding positioning value
using Gibraltar bunker or $65,500 for 55 days and a $1.56mil score with
Colombo/Gibraltar split bunkers excluding positioning value while. However,
including $275k India positioning value this ran to mid/high $60k’s basis C9.
Also, a fronthaul reported to ﬁx for 2H May dates from Pointe Noire to China –
however, rates remained unclear. Into tomorrow, further color should be added
to the basin as a tender comes to market for split dates from Narvik to Erdemir.

Panam ax/Kam sarm ax Report14th April 2026
ATL: FIRMER
PAC: FIRMER
MID EAST: FIRMER Market Comments
PAC SHORT

THE PACIFIC MARKET HAS STARTED THE WEEK ON A FIRM FOOTING, WITH OVERALL CARGO COUNT
HOLDING STEADY, AND BUILDING FURTHER AS THE WEEK PROGRESSES ON THE BACK OF STRONG
COAL ENQUIRY. EARLY IN THE WEEK, DEMAND OUT OF NOPAC GRAINS OPENED ON A QUIETER
NOTE, WHILE ACTIVITY IN THE SOUTH GAINED MOMENTUM, LED BY INDO AND AUSSIE. AS THE
WEEK HAS DEVELOPED, INDO COAL HAS DRIVEN A NOTABLE INCREASE IN CARGO VISIBILITY,
ESPECIALLY INTO CHINA, WITH ADDITIONAL SUPPORT FROM STEADY ENQUIRY INTO INDIA, WHILE
AUSSIE COAL REMAINS ACTIVE ACROSS END APRIL AND EARLY MAY POSITIONS. ON THE TONNAGE
SIDE, SUPPLY HAS REMAINED BROADLY STABLE, WITH AVAILABILITY IN LINE WITH LATE LAST WEEK
AND PROMPT VESSELS STILL PRESENT IN THE MARKET, THOUGH NOT IN EXCESS. OVERALL
DEMAND AND SUPPLY DYNAMICS ARE SUPPORTING A STEADY UPWARD PUSH, REFLECTED IN
IMPROVING SENTIMENT AND FIRMER FIXTURES, WITH PACIFIC P3 AND P5 INDICES TRENDING
POSITIVELY AS THE WEEK GETS UNDERWAY. FFA PAPER CONTINUES TO HOLD A POSITIVE TONE,
INDICATING CONFIDENCE IN NEAR-TERM MARKET STRENGTH.

1A. TRANSATLANTIC EMPLOYMENT HAS REMAINED SUBDUED, WITH DEMAND STILL SLUGGISH
AND LIMITED FIXING REPORTED. HOWEVER, LEVELS HAVE SLIGHTLY IMPROVED, SUPPORTED BY A
STRONGER OVERALL FRONT HAUL MARKET AND IMPROVING SENTIMENT. WHILE ACTIVITY IS THIN,
OWNERS ARE SHOWING RESISTANCE, AND THE ROUTE FEELS BETTER SUPPORTED THAN LAST
WEEK, WITH 1A/2A SPREAD PROVIDING SOME ADDITIONAL SUPPORT.

2A. FRONTHAUL HAS SEEN BETTER MOMENTUM, DRIVEN BY CONTINUED NCSA GRAIN DEMAND.
LEVELS HAVE TRADED UP TOWARDS USD 25,000 BKI EQUIVALENT EX ALGECIRAS, WITH USEC-INDIA
RUNS ARE TRADING RELATIVLY FLAT TO THE LONGER GRAIN EMPLOYMENT. STRONGER PAPER
MARKETS, WITH NOTABLE GAINS IN TUESDAY’S SESSION, ARE PROVIDING ADDITIONAL SUPPORT.

P6. THE SOUTH ATLANTIC HAS SEEN IMPROVED ACTIVITY, WITH AROUND TEN FIXTURES REPORTED
ACROSS MONDAY AND TUESDAY. LEVELS HAVE PUSHED HIGHER FOR END-APRIL / 1H MAY DATES,
WITH LAST DONE NOW AROUND USD 19,500 P6 EQUIVALENT. A THIN TONNAGE LIST CONTINUES
TO SUPPORT THE ROUTE.

OUTLOOK.
THE MARKET REMAINS WELL SUPPORTED. STRONG PACIFIC CONDITIONS ARE LIMITING
BALLASTERS INTO THE P6 FOR SECOND HALF MAY, WHILE THE NORTH ATLANTIC TONNAGE
LIST REMAINS MANAGEABLE. PROVIDED CURRENT DEMAND HOLDS, OUTLOOK REMAINS
POSITIIVE.

Handysize/Supramax Report14th April 2026
63,500 Atlantic: FIRMER      Paciﬁc: FIRMER           38,000 Atlantic: FLAT      Paciﬁc: FLAT
Market Comments
ATLANTIC:
On the Continent, the market remains muted, although levels are holding relatively ﬁrm.
On the Handysize market, a few scrap cargoes into the Mediterranean have entered the
market, with discussions around USD 14,000-15,000, though rates have yet to be secured.
On the Supramax and Ultramax market, Trans-Atlantic trips are ﬁxing in the USD 10,000-
11,000 range, in line with levels seen last week. In the Mediterranean Handysize market,
there has been a slight pickup in activity this week, with increased cargo enquiry, though
not enough to shift overall momentum. We are seeing owners rating Trans-Atlantic trips to
Brazil on large Handysizes at around USD 9,500, in line with levels seen last week, versus
charterer ideas closer to USD 6,500. On the Supramax and Ultramax market, activity
remains very quiet, with some vessels ballasting towards the West Mediterranean in search
of better opportunities. Trans-Atlantic trips are being discussed at around USD 9,000, in line
with levels seen at the end of last week, although rates have yet to be secured at these
levels. The West Africa market feels dead with very little ﬁxing reported, leaving owners
searching for direction. Interestingly, the ECSA Front Haul is commanding healthy levels,
prompting a wave of ballasters from the Mediterranean as those returns now look far more
attractive than anything available locally. However, the ECSA outlook for early May is
becoming crowded; a cluster of arriving vessels is set to meet a relatively thin cargo list,
which may test the current rate strength. In contrast to the quiet elsewhere, the USG
Handysize segment is looking busy, showing a decent level of underlying support. The week
started on a positive note, with owners keeping the momentum from a slight increase in
rates. Fresh cargoes have come into the market, helping to balance fundamentals,
although it’s still too early to say if this will hold. For now, there are noticeable gaps
between charterers’ and owners’ expectations. The week began with a positive vibe in the
Us Gulf and with a little ﬁxing yesterday there is a ﬁrmness with more end April enquiry
especially for ta. The list of supra/ultra tonnage for the end of April is not that long so some
market recovery after the Greek Easter.
PACIFIC:
This week, the Paciﬁc market was relatively quiet. We did not seem abundant tnng
spplyment, but cargo volumes were also limited. Market exchanges were few on Monday,
but overall owners' sentiment remained optimistic, with oﬀers staying high. However,
charterers' bids have not caught up. In SEA, coal market sentiment turned quite positive on
Tuesday, with some Indo/SEA-China cargoes come out. Nevertheless, charterers' bids have
not increased yet. Chtrs bid for an SMX open in Indo are around 14k for trip to China and
15k for trip to Thailand. Rates for China-bound routes remain lower than those for
SEA. Aussie cargoes generally feel short of tnng supply. On Monday, a spot UMX open in
Merak ﬁxed at 19k DOP for an Aussie cargo. Due to the limited tnng, the overall sentiment
in SEA remains quite positive. In the Fareast, the general cargo segment for the BH biz
remained very active this week. Prompt tonnage in NChina still limited, and general cargo
continued to indic good rates. An SMX can easily get around 17kish for general cargo to the
Med, with a premium still obtainable via Goa. Even some cargo to WAFR have been ﬁxed
at 17kish. In the Nopac market, oﬀers for cargoes have also increased. Grain cargoes are
now runing a Japan-based UMX around 17kish, showing a clear improvement compared to
last week. In ECI, some prompt vessels are available. Local iron ore is oﬀering around 13K
for a UMX for ECI iore to China. Given positive expectations in SEA and similar levels
achievable for Australia, some owners prefer to ballast to Singapore to seek more
opportunities. Local cargo export volumes from WCI remained limited, and conditions were
generally moderate. SAFR overall showed no downward trend, with a ﬁrm market. The
overall Indian Ocean situation remains one of both risks and opportunities. Some owners
prefer short voyages within the Indian Ocean, both for high rates and to bet on the future
Indian Ocean market. In summary, although the week started quietly, sentiment remains
relatively positive. We look forward to seeing how the market performs going forward.

items.parsed_text: Capesize Report14th April 2026 PAC: Firming ATL: Very Busy Market Comments After all majors remained unfixed yesterday – the basin welcomed three majors out of West Australia today and one out of TRMT to kick off activity. Initially, same levels as yesterday were offered with $13.00’s being seen by the majors – until finally first to fix was the Dampier major for 28/30 April dates at $12.80. meanwhile, a major out of Hedland was rumored to have concluded at $13.00 and an operator for 27/29 April was last bidding $12.50 and fixed at an undisclosed rate. Additionally, the major out of TMRT fixed their stem for 22/24 April at high $8.00’s for a trip to Bohadopi. Positivity from yesterday trickled into this morning with paper gaining momentum and immense volumes concluded early doors out of the South. The main focus from the get go was once again mid-May dates with a trader fixing at $31.75 until these dates were then fixed again a handful of times by traders at $31.50 with one Greek owners vessel securing $32.00. Additionally, a Newcastlemax fixed for delivery Mundra 20 April via Brazil for redelivery China at $43,500 - equivalent to around high $30s on C3 basis. Much like the other basins, the North Atlantic saw activity pick up. A trip from Nouadhibou to Arzew for 01/10 May fixed at $8.40 which as a Gibraltar round voyage ran to around mid $32k’s. Into the afternoon, a North Atlantic vessel took an end-users cargo out of Kamsar at $28 for 03/09 May. This ran to $69,750 for 55 days and a $1.8mil score excluding positioning value using Gibraltar bunker or $65,500 for 55 days and a $1.56mil score with Colombo/Gibraltar split bunkers excluding positioning value while. However, including $275k India positioning value this ran to mid/high $60k’s basis C9. Also, a fronthaul reported to fix for 2H May dates from Pointe Noire to China – however, rates remained unclear. Into tomorrow, further color should be added to the basin as a tender comes to market for split dates from Narvik to Erdemir. items.parsed_text: Panam ax/Kamsarmax Report14th April 2026 ATL: FIRMER PAC: FIRMER MID EAST: FIRMER Market Comments PAC SHORT THE PACIFIC MARKET HAS STARTED THE WEEK ON A FIRM FOOTING, WITH OVERALL CARGO COUNT HOLDING STEADY, AND BUILDING FURTHER AS THE WEEK PROGRESSES ON THE BACK OF STRONG COAL ENQUIRY. EARLY IN THE WEEK, DEMAND OUT OF NOPAC GRAINS OPENED ON A QUIETER NOTE, WHILE ACTIVITY IN THE SOUTH GAINED MOMENTUM, LED BY INDO AND AUSSIE. AS THE WEEK HAS DEVELOPED, INDO COAL HAS DRIVEN A NOTABLE INCREASE IN CARGO VISIBILITY, ESPECIALLY INTO CHINA, WITH ADDITIONAL SUPPORT FROM STEADY ENQUIRY INTO INDIA, WHILE AUSSIE COAL REMAINS ACTIVE ACROSS END APRIL AND EARLY MAY POSITIONS. ON THE TONNAGE SIDE, SUPPLY HAS REMAINED BROADLY STABLE, WITH AVAILABILITY IN LINE WITH LATE LAST WEEK AND PROMPT VESSELS STILL PRESENT IN THE MARKET, THOUGH NOT IN EXCESS. OVERALL DEMAND AND SUPPLY DYNAMICS ARE SUPPORTING A STEADY UPWARD PUSH, REFLECTED IN IMPROVING SENTIMENT AND FIRMER FIXTURES, WITH PACIFIC P3 AND P5 INDICES TRENDING POSITIVELY AS THE WEEK GETS UNDERWAY. FFA PAPER CONTINUES TO HOLD A POSITIVE TONE, INDICATING CONFIDENCE IN NEAR-TERM MARKET STRENGTH. 1A. TRANSATLANTIC EMPLOYMENT HAS REMAINED SUBDUED, WITH DEMAND STILL SLUGGISH AND LIMITED FIXING REPORTED. HOWEVER, LEVELS HAVE SLIGHTLY IMPROVED, SUPPORTED BY A STRONGER OVERALL FRONT HAUL MARKET AND IMPROVING SENTIMENT. WHILE ACTIVITY IS THIN, OWNERS ARE SHOWING RESISTANCE, AND THE ROUTE FEELS BETTER SUPPORTED THAN LAST WEEK, WITH 1A/2A SPREAD PROVIDING SOME ADDITIONAL SUPPORT. 2A. FRONTHAUL HAS SEEN BETTER MOMENTUM, DRIVEN BY CONTINUED NCSA GRAIN DEMAND. LEVELS HAVE TRADED UP TOWARDS USD 25,000 BKI EQUIVALENT EX ALGECIRAS, WITH USEC-INDIA RUNS ARE TRADING RELATIVLY FLAT TO THE LONGER GRAIN EMPLOYMENT. STRONGER PAPER MARKETS, WITH NOTABLE GAINS IN TUESDAY’S SESSION, ARE PROVIDING ADDITIONAL SUPPORT. P6. THE SOUTH ATLANTIC HAS SEEN IMPROVED ACTIVITY, WITH AROUND TEN FIXTURES REPORTED ACROSS MONDAY AND TUESDAY. LEVELS HAVE PUSHED HIGHER FOR END-APRIL / 1H MAY DATES, WITH LAST DONE NOW AROUND USD 19,500 P6 EQUIVALENT. A THIN TONNAGE LIST CONTINUES TO SUPPORT THE ROUTE. OUTLOOK. THE MARKET REMAINS WELL SUPPORTED. STRONG PACIFIC CONDITIONS ARE LIMITING BALLASTERS INTO THE P6 FOR SECOND HALF MAY, WHILE THE NORTH ATLANTIC TONNAGE LIST REMAINS MANAGEABLE. PROVIDED CURRENT DEMAND HOLDS, OUTLOOK REMAINS POSITIIVE. items.parsed_text: 14th April 2026 Iron Ore TSI 62%: - - TSI Premium Coking Coal: - - Brent UK Oil: 95.98 -3.38 EUA: 73.49 2.28 BDI 2,354 104 BCI 180 3,671 234 BPI 1,900 38 BSI 1,344 24 BHSI 706 5 Market Fundamentals CMRG-BHP Deal Reported China's state iron ore buyer CMRG has reportedly lifted a six- month procurement ban on BHP's key Pilbara grades following high-level talks between BHP's outgoing CEO Mike Henry, incoming CEO Brandon Craig and China Baowu's chairman in Shanghai, newswires report. CMRG, established in 2022 to centralise iron ore buying and extract better terms from miners, had progressively tightened curbs since September 2025. The resolution likely involves pricing concessions, with rivals Rio Tinto and Fortescue already trialling alternative indexes. The ban had contributed to spot market tightness despite record portside stockpiles, keeping seaborne iron ore above the $100/t psychological floor. BHP shares rallied 3.8% on the news while Singapore Exchange benchmark May iron ore was trading at $103.5/t, down 1.2% on the day. Chinese Dry Bulk Trade Chinese iron ore imports rose 10.8 Mt from the same period last year to 104.7 Mt in March, bringing first quarter imports 29.4 Mt higher than last year at 314.8 Mt, preliminary customs data show. Coal imports edged 0.3 Mt higher year-on-year to 39.1 Mt, with 1q26 imports up 1.5 Mt on the year at 116.3 Mt. First quarter steel imports eased 0.2 Mt on the year to 1.3 Mt while exports fell 2.7 Mt to 24.7 Mt. Meanwhile, soybean imports lifted 0.5 Mt on the year to 4.0 Mt in March, although posted an equivalent decline to 16.6 Mt in the first three months of the year. Trading Commentary Cape The cape curve pushed up today on the back of higher physical fixtures particularly on c3 and in the Atlantic. Apr traded from a low of 29000 up to a high of 30000 settling around 29800, May moved up from 32250 to 33750. Jun also improved from 32500 to 33600, with Q2 trading 31000 to 32200. Further out, Q3 went from 30400 to 31000, while Q4 moved up from 30350 to 30900. On the back end, Cal 27 traded between 25750 and 25900, with Cal 28 printing twice around 23300. Overall, it was a strong day for capes, with improvements seen right across the curve. PMX PMX papers saw an active session today, with prices pushing higher across the curve. Apr traded from a low of 17450 in the morning being paid up to 17650, while May improved from 19400 to 19675. Jun also pushed higher from 19650 to 19900, with Q2 trading 18750 to 19100, Q3 went from 18600 to 18900, while Q4 moved up from 17100 to 17300. On the back end, Cal 27 traded between 14825 and 14900, with Cal 28 trading around 13900, improving around 50 on the day, and Cal 29 printing once at 13650. Overall, the market saw a firm move higher across the curve, with good participation through the session. SMX + HANDY The SMX market was well supported as the curve stepped up amid robust buying interest over the day. Apr traded 15450 – 15600, May 17100 – 17400, Jun 16950 – 17350 and the Q2 16550 – 16750. Q3 changed hands between 16500 – 16700, Q4 15400 and Q1 at 12000. items.parsed_text: Handysize/Supramax Report14th April 2026 63,500 Atlantic: FIRMER Pacific: FIRMER 38,000 Atlantic: FLAT Pacific: FLAT Market Comments ATLANTIC: On the Continent, the market remains muted, although levels are holding relatively firm. On the Handysize market, a few scrap cargoes into the Mediterranean have entered the market, with discussions around USD 14,000-15,000, though rates have yet to be secured. On the Supramax and Ultramax market, Trans-Atlantic trips are fixing in the USD 10,000- 11,000 range, in line with levels seen last week. In the Mediterranean Handysize market, there has been a slight pickup in activity this week, with increased cargo enquiry, though not enough to shift overall momentum. We are seeing owners rating Trans-Atlantic trips to Brazil on large Handysizes at around USD 9,500, in line with levels seen last week, versus charterer ideas closer to USD 6,500. On the Supramax and Ultramax market, activity remains very quiet, with some vessels ballasting towards the West Mediterranean in search of better opportunities. Trans-Atlantic trips are being discussed at around USD 9,000, in line with levels seen at the end of last week, although rates have yet to be secured at these levels. The West Africa market feels dead with very little fixing reported, leaving owners searching for direction. Interestingly, the ECSA Front Haul is commanding healthy levels, prompting a wave of ballasters from the Mediterranean as those returns now look far more attractive than anything available locally. However, the ECSA outlook for early May is becoming crowded; a cluster of arriving vessels is set to meet a relatively thin cargo list, which may test the current rate strength. In contrast to the quiet elsewhere, the USG Handysize segment is looking busy, showing a decent level of underlying support. The week started on a positive note, with owners keeping the momentum from a slight increase in rates. Fresh cargoes have come into the market, helping to balance fundamentals, although it’s still too early to say if this will hold. For now, there are noticeable gaps between charterers’ and owners’ expectations. The week began with a positive vibe in the Us Gulf and with a little fixing yesterday there is a firmness with more end April enquiry especially for ta. The list of supra/ultra tonnage for the end of April is not that long so some market recovery after the Greek Easter. PACIFIC: This week, the Pacific market was relatively quiet. We did not seem abundant tnng spplyment, but cargo volumes were also limited. Market exchanges were few on Monday, but overall owners' sentiment remained optimistic, with offers staying high. However, charterers' bids have not caught up. In SEA, coal market sentiment turned quite positive on Tuesday, with some Indo/SEA-China cargoes come out. Nevertheless, charterers' bids have not increased yet. Chtrs bid for an SMX open in Indo are around 14k for trip to China and 15k for trip to Thailand. Rates for China-bound routes remain lower than those for SEA. Aussie cargoes generally feel short of tnng supply. On Monday, a spot UMX open in Merak fixed at 19k DOP for an Aussie cargo. Due to the limited tnng, the overall sentiment in SEA remains quite positive. In the Fareast, the general cargo segment for the BH biz remained very active this week. Prompt tonnage in NChina still limited, and general cargo continued to indic good rates. An SMX can easily get around 17kish for general cargo to the Med, with a premium still obtainable via Goa. Even some cargo to WAFR have been fixed at 17kish. In the Nopac market, offers for cargoes have also increased. Grain cargoes are now runing a Japan-based UMX around 17kish, showing a clear improvement compared to last week. In ECI, some prompt vessels are available. Local iron ore is offering around 13K for a UMX for ECI iore to China. Given positive expectations in SEA and similar levels achievable for Australia, some owners prefer to ballast to Singapore to seek more opportunities. Local cargo export volumes from WCI remained limited, and conditions were generally moderate. SAFR overall showed no downward trend, with a firm market. The overall Indian Ocean situation remains one of both risks and opportunities. Some owners prefer short voyages within the Indian Ocean, both for high rates and to bet on the future Indian Ocean market. In summary, although the week started quietly, sentiment remains relatively positive. We look forward to seeing how the market performs going forward.
